reason: The cited evidence does not address the key premises. E1 discusses a Mg-free CrMnFeCoNi alloy and Mn depletion, not Mg-containing HEAs or Al/Cr sequestration. E2 reports good corrosion resistance in Mg-Ti-Zn alloys due to a TiO2-rich film, contradicting the premise that intermetallic formation degrades corrosion resistance, and provides no data on high-temperature oxidation or Al/Cr depletion.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight HEAs can be produced in a metastable, supersaturated solid-solution state
Thermal exposure causes decomposition via diffusion-controlled precipitation of intermetallic compounds
Precipitation sequesters passivating elements (Al, Cr) from the matrix
Sequestration disrupts formation of a continuous protective oxide scale
Disrupted oxide scale leads to measurable drop in corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance
